take_homes: The agent's output is only as specific as what I put in front of it. Generic claims are the model filling gaps in my input.
Don't trust the agent's review of its own work. Use a cold reader that has only the output, and trust my own judgment over both.
Turn what worked into a rules file, then sharpen it after each use. That file is what a teammate or a fresh agent can pick up.

monday.move: Write a rules file for the pilot-cohort brief from the last run, then have a cold reader critique the brief against it
monday.who: Me, then show the file to two people on my team
monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: The cold reader flags no claim I can't back up with a source, or I've done two rounds
monday.blocker: There is no shared place for the file; my team keeps separate copies

misconception.why: The module shows the gain comes from context and a reusable rules file that gets sharpened, not from better wording of a single prompt. I still half-think prompt skill matters, since the prompts were supplied for me.

one_line: The core idea is good: context, don't trust the agent's own review, keep a rules file. But the filler notes repeat through it and a snake game and a LinkedIn site are a long way from a pricing decision.
